summary: Fast C/C++ port of OpenAI's Whisper speech recognition model that transcribes audio on your own computer, even without a GPU.

heroCommands.command:
git clone https://github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp.git
cd whisper.cpp
sh ./models/download-ggml-model.sh base.en
cmake -B build
cmake --build build -j --config Release
./build/bin/whisper-cli -f samples/jfk.wav

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: whisper.cpp is a high-performance C/C++ implementation of OpenAI's Whisper speech recognition model. It turns speech in audio files into text locally on your own machine, with no Python and no cloud service needed.
sixtySeconds.problem: The original Whisper needs Python, PyTorch and ideally a GPU. whisper.cpp runs the same models as a small native program that works on laptops, phones and servers, including CPU-only machines.
whoFor: Apple Silicon users who want fast local transcription
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for fast, dependency-free, offline transcription with broad hardware support, from Apple Silicon and x86 CPUs to NVIDIA, AMD, Vulkan and NPUs.
requirements: Disk and memory for a model (tiny ~75 MiB up to large ~2.9 GiB)

overview: You clone the repository, download a Whisper model converted to ggml format with the included script, build with CMake and run whisper-cli on an audio file. Running make base.en downloads the base.en model and transcribes all sample .wav files in one step.

It is optimised for Apple Silicon (NEON, Accelerate, Metal, Core ML), supports AVX on x86, integer quantization and GPU backends for NVIDIA, AMD ROCm, Vulkan and more. Models range from tiny (75 MiB on disk, about 273 MB memory) to large (2.9 GiB, about 3.9 GB).
whisper-cli currently needs 16-bit WAV input, so convert other formats with ffmpeg first. The project is MIT licensed and also offers a C-style API for embedding in other software.
